sources.entry: Open-Meteo - Weather API with open-data forecasts, historical and climate data from all major national weather services. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Open-Meteo is an open-source weather API offering free non-commercial access to forecasts, historical weather, and related data built from national weather services' open model data, which can also be self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a weather API that requires no API key and supports CORS. It serves hourly forecasts up to 16 days ahead, historical weather going back 80 years, and marine, air quality, geocoding, elevation, and flood APIs. It draws on several national weather models (NOAA GFS/HRRR, DWD ICON, MeteoFrance, ECMWF IFS, JMA, GEM HRDPS, MET Norway) and stores processed data in a custom compressed time-series format. The project says it downloads and processes more than 5 TB of data daily. The API can be self-hosted with Docker or an Ubuntu 22.04 package, and it can fetch data remotely from the public database and cache it locally. The README also lists many third-party apps and client SDKs built on the API.
use_cases: get weather forecasts in an app without an API key
historical weather and climate data analysis
air quality, marine, or flood data lookups
build a weather widget or dashboard
how_to_run: docker: follow the Getting Started guide in the project documentation to launch an API instance
Ubuntu 22.04: install the prebuilt package (see Getting Started guide)
Optional: see Downloading Weather Models to maintain a local weather database
notable: No API key, cookies, ads, or tracking; CORS supported
Combines multiple national weather service models, including regional models up to 1.5 km resolution
Can run from remote public database with local caching, so full model downloads are not required
Large ecosystem of listed apps and client SDKs (Python, Go, Rust, R, TypeScript and others)
caveats: Free access is for non-commercial use; commercial use requires contacting the maintainers
Applications exceeding 10,000 requests per day must contact the project, and misuse may lead to blocking
Maintaining a full local weather database requires downloading large model data (over 5 TB processed daily upstream)
